newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Christopher in Mideast to stress urgency of talks.
newsitem.headline: Christopher in Mideast to stress urgency of talks.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher arrived in the Middle East on Sunday to urge Israelis and Palestinians to reach swift and significant results in resumed peace talks, a U.S. official said.
His plane landed in Tel Aviv for a hastily arranged visit with leaders of Israel and the Palestinians ahead of negotiations in the Palestinian-ruled Gaza Strip later in the day.

On the way to Israel, Christopher said he wanted an opportunity to meet Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Sunday to follow up on last week's emergency summit in Washington.

Christopher told reporters flying with him he wanted to stress "the importance of significant progress, the urgency of it and especially a reminder of their commitment that they would become personally involved if progress wasn't made."

U.S. President Bill Clinton, who called the summit following gunbattles and clashes unprecedented in the three years since the first Israeli-PLO peace accord, said the talks in Gaza would focus on Israel's long-delayed redeployment from Hebron.

Hebron is the last of seven West Bank cities due to have been given Palestinian self-rule under a peace deal Arafat signed with the previous Israeli government. The pullback has been delayed by Islamic suicide bombings in Israel that killed 59 people and Israeli security concerns.
